title: The Music Competition
text_content: Chioma had played the drum for many years, but never before a large audience. When her teacher announced the school music competition, her stomach filled with worry. Every evening she practised in the yard while her little brother clapped along. On the day of the competition, the hall was crowded with parents, teachers and excited children. Chioma waited backstage, holding her sticks so tightly that her fingers began to hurt. The first group performed a lively song, and everyone in the audience cheered with great enthusiasm. Her legs felt weak, and for a moment she wanted to run home. Then she remembered her teacher's advice to listen carefully to the beat. She took a slow breath, walked onto the stage, and closed her eyes. The beautiful rhythm rose from her drum, steady and strong, and the whole hall grew quiet. When she finished, there was a moment of silence, followed by a wave of applause. Chioma opened her eyes and smiled, because her nervous feeling had completely disappeared. She did not win first prize, but she knew she had gained something far more important.
